old_caption: The video captures a dynamic and vibrant scene of paint splashing into the air against a stark black background. The paint, in vivid hues of blue, green, red, and yellow, is seen in mid-air, creating an explosion of color. The paint appears to be in motion, with some streams curving gracefully while others shoot upwards, forming intricate patterns. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the paint's movement and the contrast between the bright colors and the dark backdrop. The paint droplets are scattered around the central splash, adding depth and texture to the scene. The overall effect is mesmerizing, showcasing the beauty and energy of the paint in motion.

caption: The video captures a slow-motion paint splash against a pure black background. A vertical column of blue paint streaked with red extends upward from a glossy base, crowned by two red prongs that stretch and thin only slightly. Radiating green tendrils with bulbous tips curl and elongate around the column, while a blue flap on the right contains a dark gap that changes only subtly. Scattered yellow and green droplets hang in the surrounding darkness with little visible drift. A paint-dripped rectangular block at the left edge and the translucent plastic sheet at the right appear fixed, suggesting a static camera. The crown holds its overall shape throughout, the viscous motion continuing without any new impact or collapse.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
